question: New press reports in April 2026, based on internal emails and documents included in the judicial summary of the accident in Adamuz (Córdoba) that resulted in the deaths of 46 people on 18 January 2026, show that a rail was installed in the area that had a serial number that did not appear on the manufacturer’s invoices or delivery orders.

ArcelorMittal confirmed in writing that it could not prove the traceability of this rail and recommended its immediate replacement as a preventive measure. Upon learning this information, ADIF replaced 42 metres of track and removed welds present at the time of the accident without first informing the judicial authority investigating the accident.
The investigating judge has asked for explanations in relation to the replacement and to the whereabouts of the material removed. 1.
Does the Commission consider the presence of rail infrastructure components without verified traceability on the TEN-T network to be compatible with Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2016/797?
Has Spain notified the Commission and ERA of the finding of this component in accordance with Article 11 of Directive (EU) 2016/797?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.6.2026) The Commission has not received evidence about the presence of rail infrastructure components without verified traceability on the trans-European transport (TEN-T) network.

As indicated in Article 15 of the Interoperability Directive (EU) 2016/7971, notified bodies are responsible for verifying the suitability of the components to obtain the ‘EC’ declaration and its compatibility with Article 10 of the Directive.

If a Member State finds that a structural subsystem covered by the ‘EC’ declaration of verification does not fully comply with the Interoperability Directive (EU) 2016/797, it may request that additional checks be carried out and shall inform the Commission.

It is also responsible for ensuring that a component is not placed on a line if it finds that the ‘EC’ declaration has been drawn up improperly, following Article 16 of the Interoperability Directive (EU) 2016/797.

According to Article 11 of the Interoperability Directive (EU) 2016/797, if a Member State finds that an interoperability constituent covered by the ‘EC’ declaration fails to comply with the essential requirements, it should inform the Commission and the European Union Agency for Railway (ERA) of the measures taken and give reasons for its decision.
At this moment, neither the Commission nor ERA has received such an information in relation to the Adamuz accident.
1 Directive (EU) 2016/797 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on the interoperability

of the rail system within the European Union (recast) (Text with EEA relevance). OJ L 138, 26.5.2016, pp. 44– 101 (BG, ES, CS, DA, DE, ET, EL, EN, FR, HR, IT, LV, LT, HU, MT, NL, PL, PT, RO, SK, SL, FI, SV).
